quote: FAME (FActual Multi-task model Editing) is a benchmark comprising 128k factual data items. We utilize these data items to construct both single-hop and multi-hop questions. For single-hop questions, we include six forms: QA, sentence completion, cloze test, multiple-choice questions, fact check, and locality test. For multi-hop questions, we include multi-hop questions and dialogues.

“FAME comprises 128k real data items, including various tasks with singlehop and multi‑hop questions… we incorporate tasks from existing datasets like QA, fact‑check, multi‑hop QA, and introduce new tasks such as cloze and dialogue.”
Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable capabilities across various domains and are extensively utilized in practical applications.
outputs: Generated answers for questions, completions, dialogues, and fact checks.
model‑generated answers to QA, sentence completions, cloze fills, multiple‑choice selections, fact‑check judgments, and dialogue responses
The generated outputs include answers to single-hop and multi-hop questions, dialogue responses, fact verification results, cloze completions, and multiple-choice selections.

quote: We use the following metrics to evaluate whether editing achieves our goal ... Accuracy ... Locality ... SURE ... Efficiency ... Accuracy To calculate accuracy, we instruct the model to generate responses for tasks and evaluate whether they match the gold answers exactly. The resulting average accuracy is then recorded as exact match (EM). Locality Locality measures whether an editing method will influence irrelevant knowledge. We utilize drawdown (DD) to compute performance degradation and employ Neighborhood KL divergence (NKL) to measure whether the model is significantly affected. SURE ... we propose the metric SURE ... to estimate the performance of edited models in real-world scenarios.

“We calculate accuracy by instructing the model to generate responses… The resulting average accuracy is recorded as exact match (EM). We also use drawdown (DD) and Neighborhood KL divergence (NKL) as side‑effect metrics, and introduce SURE to combine accuracy and side effects.”
